findings.consequence: Line 15 is inside an italic log paragraph whose own sentences are first person ('Teague looked across the yard at the five of us going in under our own roof'), and it is the only place in the chapter, or in the B7 precedent, where the writer of the log names himself in the third person. Read aloud - which is the shipping condition - a listener hears the log's 'I' for eight paragraphs and then hears 'Cael said Noted', and the cheapest available inference is that somebody else is writing this entry. The r2 repair_target said what the sentence needed and gave the wording: 'the answer Cael's own - e.g. He said it at the plank in the snow and I said the one word back'. The canon fact was taken and the person was not: B7 Ch24:47 is close-third narration, where 'Cael said' is correct, and the clause has been lifted out of that register into a document that cannot carry it. The chapter's whole opening movement is the log; a register break in it is a break in the instrument the book has chosen to tell its winter with.

Everything else in the sentence is right and must not move - 'His term stands: spring, whatever's on that bearing, his crew comes' delivers the plant, Teague stays off the page beyond the chin-lift, none of his four is named, and Pike writes nothing under the blank season line. comparison_evidence.quote: Teague wintered at Lowmarch, as Teague's crew wintered every year, at the best table, with the jug, and he came to the plank while Pike was still standing back from the sheet, because a captain who has set a term does not wait for a better moment to say it.

findings.consequence: In Book 7 the pen goes down before Teague reaches the plank and for a different reason: Ch24:25 'Pike did not write a number', Ch24:31 'He put the pen down. He did not enter a line number', then Ch24:39 has Teague arrive while Pike is already standing back from the pinned sheet. The r3 clause reverses that, so a reader who remembers the scene sees Pike either put the pen down twice or put it down in answer to a term that was said after he had finished. The facts are individually true and the order is not, and the r2 repair_target had already named the hazard and asked for Pike to be kept out of the sentence entirely, precisely because the blank line does its work by being untouched rather than by being re-earned in front of Teague. Low rather than medium because the log is a compressed memory of an afternoon and the two beats are minutes apart, but it is a contradiction against the scene the log is remembering and it was avoidable.

concerns: The author report closes F-011 as MET with the evidence line "'Cael said Noted, and Pike put his pen down and wrote nothing under the blank season line' - B7 Ch24:31/47 honored." The two B7 lines cited are the right lines and the facts taken from them are right; what the check did not test is whether the sentence could be spoken by the document it was put into. This is the second consecutive round in which a repair closed the contradiction it was aimed at and opened a fresh one inside the same replaced string (r2: the F-005 money repair produced the F-012 garden path; r3: the F-011 attribution repair produced F-014 and F-015). A one-line register test on every replacement that lands inside an italic log paragraph - does this sentence say 'I' where the log says 'I'? - would have caught both.

Line 187's repair is correct and is harder to hear than line 31's. Line 31 gives the designation first and the stopped line after it; line 187 opens the entry, interrupts for eleven words of em-dashed parenthesis ('and under it a line that stopped, third site confirmed on bearing'), and only then delivers the appositive 'a designation, in an index, in the surveyor's own hand'. Both sentences are true and they agree, which is what the finding required; only one of them lands on a single hearing. Not a defect against any contract - the clause is Karis reporting a document, and the shape is the series' own - but if a line-edit pass touches this paragraph, this is the sentence in it.
